reviews.summary: -i is parsed and the timed host path repeats the selected actual kernel call until its counter reaches the iteration bound. Dispatch is mean row length: short rows launch one thread per row; otherwise grouped warps cover all rows. SASS for both variants has CSR global loads, FP64 multiplication and accumulation, CSR/tile loop backedges and output stores. No graph or persistent-device iteration loop is used.

source_evidence.claim: The short kernel walks offsets[row]..offsets[row+1] and stores each row; grouped kernel tiles that same interval and stores from lane 0. The parsed iteration count wraps either all-row launch, selected at mean-length 16.

compiled_evidence.claim: For the short path, host counter increment/limit check branches to exit, then call to the short-row device stub returns to that check. The grouped path likewise increments/checks its counter and calls grouped stub before returning to the check.

Grouped and short-row functions show global input activity, FP64 product/accumulation, loop branches through the row/tile traversal, and row output stores (grouped 855, short 1060). These correspond to both source dispatch variants.

reviews.notes: Static native SASS is the available artifact; no runtime/JIT execution was authorized or performed. Work-count conclusion is about source dispatch and emitted variants, not runtime rank/input validation.

reviews.summary: The timed wrapper has separate iterations loops for warp and sliced-CSR dispatch, and both host loops are present in native assembly with counter backedges around actual device stubs. The warp path walks CSR entries in tiles; the sliced path iterates each row's full recorded length. Both emit FP64 arithmetic, loop branches and per-row stores. No graph/persistent loop is used.

source_evidence.claim: Both device strategies cover every row, traverse either CSR offsets or each sliced-row length, accumulate products and store output; the timed path repeats whichever strategy dispatch selects for each iteration.

compiled_evidence.claim: Warp path increments and checks its timed counter, calls the warp device stub, then returns to the counter check; stop event/synchronization follows. Sliced path does the same around the sliced kernel stub.
Warp kernel has FP64 products and accumulation, tile/control-flow backedges and output store. Sliced CSR kernel likewise has FP64 multiply/add, row traversal backedges and output store.

reviews.notes: Host resolves the selected kernel and synchronizes before/after timing; JIT/module loading is deliberately outside timing. No graph or persistent loop observed.

reviews.summary: -i reaches a per-width benchmark function; main dispatches among widths 1,4,8,16,32 by mean row length. Each emitted host specialization has an iteration counter/backedge around cudaLaunchKernel. Each device specialization walks the row CSR interval by lane stride, reduces lane sums and stores the row result. No device persistent loop or graph is used.

source_evidence.claim: Kernel lanes stride through each row's CSR entries, reduce, and one lane stores output; benchmark loops over requested iterations, and main selects Width 1/4/8/16/32 from mean row length and passes iterations.

compiled_evidence.claim: The five benchmark specializations respectively call cudaLaunchKernel inside a counter loop that compares against the iteration bound and branches back; main's function-pointer setup selects these specialization functions based on the computed mean-length thresholds.

All five emitted widths contain entry/indexed global loads, double FMA accumulation, loop/reduction control flow and a per-row STG output (ends at 595, 1242, 1893, 2550, 3205 respectively). These are the five dispatched implementations.

reviews.notes: Compiled native launch loops and all width-specific SASS bodies were inspected. SASS establishes the emitted implementation; dynamic library/JIT behavior was not executed.

reviews.summary: The selected runIterations<Width> is called from source dispatch by average row length and loops over requested iterations, launching once on each trip. Native code has the counter and actual CUDA launch/backedge in each of four instantiated widths (1,4,8,32). Each SASS variant processes batch, full-width remainder and tail entries before storing output. No graph/persistent loop.

source_evidence.claim: Kernel traverses row CSR entries in batches plus full-width remainder and tail, then stores output; runIterations invokes it once per requested iteration; dispatch passes iterations into Width 1/4/8/32 choice.

compiled_evidence.claim: Each of four runIterations specializations records timing and contains actual cudaLaunchKernel followed by increment/compare and a backedge until the passed limit; main selects the specialization by mean nonzeros per row and calls the selected function.

Each emitted width implementation includes FP64 product/accumulation, traversal branches/backedges for chunks and remainder/tail, and a global output store; all four source-dispatched widths are represented.

reviews.notes: Static SASS/native disassembly checked; no compile/runtime/JIT experiment. Repeated output overwrite does not remove the arithmetic in subsequent launches.

reviews.summary: Rows are divided into contiguous rank intervals by boundary(dim, rank, ranks), and each rank uploads its local CSR-derived packed rows. Timed local loop repeats the multiply kernel for iterations. Device code loads each local row's packed slice/length, batches eight products, processes the tail, accumulates and stores. No graph/persistent kernel loop.

source_evidence.claim: Boundary formulas and transfers give each rank its local rows/CSR data; packed kernel walks lengths for each row and stores output; -i is parsed and local GPU launch is repeated iterations times.

compiled_evidence.claim: Native run loop initializes counter, forms the multiply launch configuration, calls its actual device stub, increments/checks against the iteration limit and branches back; completion path checks launch and synchronizes.
Emitted kernel bounds-checks row id, performs packed input loads and FP64 multiply/add in batch and tail, loops while work remains, and stores result[row].

reviews.notes: MPI rank coverage and transfers are source-level (not run); kernel's local-row work and timed repeat are directly visible in native/device dumps.

reviews.summary: Ranks use contiguous [boundary(rank), boundary(rank+1)) row intervals and gather those intervals back to the global output. The source dispatches Width 1 or 8. Native host code retains the selected-function call inside the iterations counter/backedge; device variants load CSR offsets/entries, multiply and reduce products, and store each local row. No graph/persistent loop.

source_evidence.claim: Per-rank CSR construction/rebasing covers its assigned rows, run selects lanes and computes the complete local row domain, repeats launch by iterations, then gathers using matching rank boundaries.

compiled_evidence.claim: Native run selects one of the two kernel functions before timing; timed loop invokes the selected function pointer, increments/checks iteration bound and returns to launch setup. Kernel wrapper specializations call cudaLaunchKernel.
Width-8 and Width-1 kernels contain FP64 multiplies, accumulation/reduction, entry-loop backedges and output stores at 497 and 1532 respectively.

reviews.notes: Rank interval and gather semantics assessed statically; no MPI execution. Kernel function pointer targets the two emitted width variants; no graph/persistent loop observed.

reviews.summary: Source builds row/entry cuts and distributes CSR slices over ranks. Each rank runs a host iteration loop around multiply for all local rows; native run has actual multiply stub call inside a counter/backedge to the iteration limit. The kernel traverses each local packed row's full length and writes its result. No graph/persistent loop.

source_evidence.claim: Kernel maps threads over all local rows, traverses lengths and stores output; rowCuts/entryCuts partition and distribute the matrix; timed path repeats the kernel launch exactly iterations times.

compiled_evidence.claim: After pre-timing device synchronization/barrier and start time, native loop calculates grid, issues multiply device stub, increments/checks iteration counter and returns to launch; after loop it synchronizes before ending timing.
Kernel performs row-index/bounds work, global loads, double multiply/add, row-entry backedges and stores one output per row.

reviews.notes: MPI data partition is established by source cuts/distribution, not runtime execution. No launch graph or device-persistent loop present.

reviews.summary: Ranks own contiguous row ranges computed from numRows*proc/ranks, with globally generated CSR data rebased to local offsets. Timed host loop launches the spmv kernel once per iteration; native code shows counter/backedge around the actual device stub then device synchronization. Kernel traverses each packed row length, accumulates FP64 products and stores output. No graph/persistent loop.

source_evidence.claim: Local row boundaries and CSR rebasing define a complete rank-owned row interval; kernel iterates its row length and stores output; timed loop repeats launch by parsed -i count and gathers local outputs afterward.

compiled_evidence.claim: Native timed path increments and checks counter, invokes actual spmv device stub and branches back until the limit, then checks launch and synchronizes. Stub dispatches through cudaLaunchKernel.
Kernel's row bounds and packed-row input loads precede FP64 product/accumulation; loop branches cover row entries and final STG stores result.
